summary: Amersfoort (about 163,000 residents) is bringing in paid and permit parking in phases after a contested process: an advisory referendum in November 2023 went against the plan by about 74 percent (80 percent turnout, according to NOS), but the council approved a phased version on 22 April 2025. Phase 1 began on 1 October 2025 with permit-only parking in Kruiskamp, Gildekwartier, Hoefkwartier and parts of Vermeerkwartier and Randenbroek, and paid parking along part of the Leusderweg. Phase 2, announced in December 2025 for 1 October 2026, is not in force as announced: after the March 2026 council elections the city postponed Soesterkwartier, Isselt, Eemkwartier, De Koppel and Liendert, and only Jericho and Jeruzalem were formally set to start on 1 October 2026 (we did not find a report confirming the start). The northern districts including Hoogland are due to stay free until at least 2035. The centre has been car-light since January 2021. Street tariffs listed on 21 October 2026 include a day-ticket zone (3 euros for the first hour, then 60 euros a day), 3 euros an hour in hourly zones and 0.30 euros an hour for two hours in shopping areas, and the three central garages run by Coöperatie ParkeerService charge 2.61 to 3.24 euros an hour and 16.22 euros a day (Amerena 0.70 euros for the first 8 hours); Q-Park, P1, Parkking and Arrivee run other garages. The July 2026 coalition agreement plans, but has not yet implemented, scrapping the day ticket, 12 euros an hour for long street stays near the centre, free first two hours in shopping areas, lower some tariffs, adjusted phasing and a smart system with signs showing garage availability. Audit-office findings from December 2021 about garage capacity and limited occupancy data are old.

items.text: The car-light historic centre took effect on 4 January 2021: access needs an exemption, street parking there is permit-only and 71 paid street spaces were removed, while residents' visitors get a reduced rate in the municipal garages. The audit office asked whether this use of municipal garages complies with the Dutch Market and Government Act, as the city competes with private operators; the municipality said it would test this.
items.source_title: Rekenkamer Amersfoort, Parkeergarages en fietsenstallingen Amersfoort (report, 6 Dec 2021)

items.text: A December 2021 audit report by the city's audit office counted 13 public garages with 4,571 spaces (garages in use on 1 December 2019), nine of them in and around the centre with 3,974 spaces. The three municipal centre garages (Koestraat, Stadhuisplein, Flintplein, run by Coöperatie ParkeerService) had 930 spaces (23.4 percent); Q-Park (counted together with P1 in the report's table) was the largest provider with 1,819 spaces (45.9 percent). These figures are old; current garage capacities differ slightly.
items.source_title: Rekenkamer Amersfoort, Parkeergarages en fietsenstallingen Amersfoort (report, 6 Dec 2021)

items.text: In its formal response to the December 2021 audit, the municipality said it stopped its dynamic parking route information system in 2016. Attempts to keep it going with private garages had stalled by 2014, partly because of apps, and research had shown that displaying numbers of free spaces had almost no effect on garage choice; the audit report adds that high costs and operators no longer willing to contribute were also behind the decision. The municipality said it would look with operators at better opening of digital open parking data for parking apps.
items.source_title: Rekenkamer Amersfoort audit report (Dec 2021) and the municipality's formal response (Bestuurlijke reactie)

items.text: The December 2021 audit found the municipality had only limited occupancy information even for its own garages and no good picture of occupancy in the private garages, and that no information on occupancy rates was shared between the municipality and the private operators. It expected parking pressure to rise in the municipal garages because of the car-light centre, but said it was unclear whether they had enough capacity, since part of their spaces was already taken by subscription holders.
items.source_title: Rekenkamer Amersfoort, Parkeergarages en fietsenstallingen Amersfoort (report, 6 Dec 2021) (summary and chapter 4)

items.text: In November 2023 residents rejected the planned paid-parking policy in an advisory referendum, with about three quarters voting against. The council nevertheless discussed the policy further and amended it.
items.source_title: RTV Utrecht, 1,5 jaar na 'nee' bij referendum is betaald parkeren in Amersfoort een feit

items.text: The council approved the new parking policy on 22 April 2025 by a large majority, to be introduced in phases from October 2025: first resident permit 30 euros a year, second 300 euros in the centre or 150 at the edge, visitors at most 1.20 euros a day. Care-giver permits were cut to 30 euros by unanimous vote.
items.source_title: RTV Utrecht, 1,5 jaar na 'nee' bij referendum is betaald parkeren in Amersfoort een feit

items.text: Phase 1 of paid and permit parking started on 1 October 2025. From that morning residents of Kruiskamp, Gildekwartier, Hoefkwartier, Zonnehof, Hogekwartier and part of Vermeerkwartier and Randenbroek could park on the street only with a permit, and paying began at more places, including along part of the Leusderweg shopping street. RTV Utrecht reported that the last phase was planned for October 2027 and that Kattenbroek, Hoogland, Nieuwland, Vathorst (except Bovenduist) and Hooglanderveen would in any case not move to paid parking until 2035.
items.source_title: RTV Utrecht, Betalen voor parkeren breidt uit: dit verandert in Amersfoort

items.text: On 11 December 2025 the alderman told the council in a letter that phase 2, planned for 1 February 2026, would move to 1 October 2026 for Soesterkwartier, Isselt, Eemkwartier and Jeruzalem, that Liendert would start on 1 October 2026 because of its planned redevelopment, and that Randenbroek, Rustenburg and Amersfoort Zuid would follow on 1 May 2027. This planning was later overtaken: on 8 April 2026, after the March 2026 council elections, the city postponed paid parking in Soesterkwartier, Isselt, Eemkwartier, De Koppel and Liendert for the time being, keeping 1 October 2026 only for Jericho and Jeruzalem.
items.source_title: ParkeerService Amersfoort, Invoeren betaald parkeren (11 Dec 2025), with RTV Utrecht, Amersfoort stopt voorlopig met uitbreiding betaald parkeren (8 April 2026)

items.text: NOS reported on 14 March 2026, ahead of the March 2026 council elections, that two local parties had been founded in protest against the paid-parking policy. Alderman Tyas Bijlholt said the tariffs are needed because the city is growing from 163,000 to 190,000 residents and the roads are already busy. A cheese seller on the Leusderweg said his customers were positive, while a baker at a shopping centre reported 30 percent lower turnover than a year earlier. NOS also gave 74 percent of voters against the plan in the referendum, on an 80 percent turnout.
items.source_title: NOS, Parkeren als verdienmodel? In Amersfoort zijn twee partijen ontstaan uit verzet

items.text: The July 2026 coalition agreement (PRO, KeiHart voor Amersfoort, D66, VVD, CDA) states intentions to abolish the day ticket, allow short street parking at a reasonable rate in the ring around the car-light centre but charge 12 euros an hour for longer stays, make the first two hours free in shopping areas that already have regulated parking, lower some parking and permit tariffs, and adjust the earlier phasing of paid-parking expansion. It also says parking pressure in surrounding areas will be measured about half a year after introduction, with regulation introduced where it exceeds 90 percent. These are plans, not rules in force.

The coalition agreement wants visitors to use garages in the centre, states that a garage should always be cheaper than the street, and plans digital signs on the ring roads and a smart digital system showing garage availability. These are plans; no system was found in operation.

Street tariffs shown on 21 October 2026 (listed as per 1 January 2026): day-ticket zone 3 euros for the first hour then 60 euros for a day, hourly zones 3 euros an hour, shopping areas 0.30 euros per hour for two hours. Charging hours in the day-ticket and hourly zones are Monday-Saturday 09:00-24:00 and Sunday 12:00-24:00; the page was read on 21 October 2026.

Garage tariffs listed for 2026 and read on 21 October 2026: Koestraat and Stadhuisplein 3.24 euros per hour and 16.22 euros per day, Flintplein 2.61 euros per hour and 16.22 per day, charged per 20 minutes. Amerena costs 0.70 euros for the first 8 hours, then 0.03 euros per minute.

Permit tariffs for the year 1 October to 1 October stay unchanged: first resident permit 30 euros, second 300 or 150 euros by zone, third 600 or 300 euros; the digital visitor scheme costs 0.30 euros per hour up to 1.20 euros a day. Page read on 21 October 2026.

The four municipality-linked garages are run by Coöperatie ParkeerService and are open 24/7: Koestraat 406 spaces (4 charge points), Flintplein 347 (5), Amerena 218 (2), Stadhuisplein 177 (5). They use licence-plate recognition at exit and accept mobile payment; Flintplein, Stadhuisplein and Amerena take cards only. Pages read on 21 October 2026.
items.source_title: ParkeerService Amersfoort, garage pages (Koestraat, Flintplein, Stadhuisplein, Amerena)

items.text: Other garages listed by ParkeerService on 21 October 2026: Eemplein 625 spaces (managed by Parkking, entry 07:00-01:00), Q-Park Mondriaan 575, St. Jorisplein 462 and Beestenmarkt 365, P1 Asch van Wijckstraat 450, Arrivee Neptunusplein 84. The city lists 15 garages and P+R sites including Oppidium, Emiclaer, De Argonaut and De Nieuwe Hof.
items.source_title: ParkeerService Amersfoort, garage pages and gemeente Amersfoort, Parkeergarages in Amersfoort

items.text: The city says one public charge-point operator is currently active, although charge points of several operators remain from earlier cooperation. It places new points based on usage data and takes grid congestion into account, and the pay or permit duty continues to apply while charging in paid or permit zones. Charging prices are set by the charge-point owner and the company that issued the charge pass, not by the city. Page read on 21 October 2026.
items.source_title: gemeente Amersfoort, Opladen elektrische auto's / Parkeren

items.text: Amersfoort has three P+R sites near stations: Barchman Wuytierslaan, Piet Mondriaanplein and Station Schothorst. Rail travellers get a daily discount; P+R Schothorst now falls within paid parking Monday-Friday 23:00-06:00 at 3 euros an hour. Page read on 21 October 2026.

Q-Park pages for Amersfoort garages returned 404; no Q-Park tariff or occupancy data found. Hendrik Wiersma garage and a Hoogland station-area car park were not found in any opened source (Hoogland appears only as a district excluded from paid parking until 2035).

No garage occupancy, utilisation statistics or open-data/guidance system statements after 2021 were found; the 2021 audit says the municipality had little occupancy data. No 2026 council papers (raadsinformatie) were opened, and no data on the Eemplein/Parkking tariffs.

Web search budget was used up before searches on new or closed car parks, station-area projects and RTV Utrecht follow-ups could be run, so developments in garage construction or refurbishment (apart from the 2021 Stadhuisplein lift credit) are not covered.
